meta.title: Breakout: Shifts in Voice and Mood

questions.prompt: Model text: The coach selected the squad. Which rewritten sentence changes the active voice to passive voice?
choices: The coach chose the squad.
The squad was selected by the coach.
The squad selected the coach.
The coach was selected by the squad.
questions.explanation: The rewritten sentence makes the squad the subject of a passive construction while the coach remains the doer of the action.
questions.skill: Recognize an active-to-passive revision
questions.topic: Notice It in a Model Text - Shifts in Voice and Mood

questions.prompt: Read this passage: Close the window before the storm arrives. The forecast predicts heavy rain tonight. What shift in mood occurs between the two sentences?
choices: Indicative mood to subjunctive mood
Imperative mood to subjunctive mood
Active voice to passive voice
Imperative mood to indicative mood
questions.explanation: The first sentence gives a command in the imperative mood, while the second makes a factual statement in the indicative mood.
questions.skill: Identify an imperative-to-indicative mood shift
questions.topic: Notice It in a Model Text - Shifts in Voice and Mood

questions.prompt: Which rewrite changes the passive sentence The essay was submitted by Jonah into active voice while keeping the simple past tense and the original meaning?
choices: Jonah submitted the essay.
Jonah was submitting the essay.
Jonah has submitted the essay.
Jonah will submit the essay.
questions.explanation: Jonah submitted the essay makes Jonah the subject and keeps the sentence in active voice and simple past tense.
questions.skill: Rewrite a passive sentence in active voice
questions.topic: Activity 1 of 9 (quiz/game): Notice It in a Model Text - Shifts in Voice and Mood

questions.prompt: Read this passage: Submit all forms before noon. Were I the manager, I would extend the deadline until Friday. What shift occurs between the two sentences?
choices: Imperative mood to subjunctive mood
Indicative mood to imperative mood
Active voice to passive voice
Subjunctive mood to indicative mood
questions.explanation: The first sentence uses imperative mood to give a command, and the second shifts to subjunctive mood to express a hypothetical situation.
questions.skill: Identifying shifts in voice and mood
questions.topic: Notice It in a Model Text - Shifts in Voice and Mood

questions.prompt: Follow the marked path. The trail continues beyond the ridge. Which pair preserves the mood progression of the text?
choices: Check the map. The route ends at the lake.
The route ends at the lake. Check the map.
If the route had ended at the lake, we would have taken the path.
Open the gate. Keep it closed.
questions.explanation: The pair moves from a command in the imperative mood to a factual statement in the indicative mood, as the text does.
questions.skill: Track a shift from imperative to indicative mood
questions.topic: Activity 1 of 9 (quiz/game): Notice It in a Model Text - Shifts in Voice and Mood

questions.prompt: Which sentence pair contains a shift from active voice to passive voice?
choices: The catalog was updated by the librarian. The librarian updated it yesterday.
The librarian updated the catalog. The catalog was updated by the librarian.
The librarian updated the catalog. The catalog listed new arrivals.
The librarian updated the catalog. The visitors consulted the new listings.
questions.explanation: The first sentence makes the librarian the doer, while the second makes the catalog the subject of a passive construction.
questions.skill: Identifying an active-to-passive voice shift
questions.topic: Notice It in a Model Text - Shifts in Voice and Mood

questions.prompt: The package was checked by the clerk. If the address were correct, the clerk would release it. Which option matches the first sentence's voice and the second sentence's mood and main-clause voice?
choices: The ticket was inspected by the agent. If the name had been valid, the pass would have been issued by the agent.
The agent inspected the ticket. If the name were valid, the agent would issue the pass.
The ticket was inspected by the agent. The name is valid, so the agent issued the pass.
The ticket was inspected by the agent. If the name were valid, the agent would issue the pass.
questions.explanation: The first sentence is passive, while the second shifts to a subjunctive condition whose main clause gives the agent active voice.
questions.skill: Distinguish passive voice from a subjunctive conditional
questions.topic: Activity 1 of 9 (quiz/game): Notice It in a Model Text - Shifts in Voice and Mood

questions.prompt: Read this passage: The new bridge was completed last spring. City officials celebrated the opening yesterday. What shift occurs between the two sentences?
choices: Subjunctive mood to imperative mood
Active voice to passive voice
Indicative mood to subjunctive mood
Passive voice to active voice
questions.explanation: The first sentence is written in passive voice because the bridge receives the action, and the second shifts to active voice because the officials perform it.
questions.skill: Identifying shifts in voice and mood
questions.topic: Notice It in a Model Text - Shifts in Voice and Mood

questions.prompt: Read this passage: The pottery was fired by Ada. Ada inspected each piece before it was displayed. What shift occurs between the two sentences?
choices: Passive voice to active voice
Active voice to passive voice
Indicative mood to subjunctive mood
Imperative mood to indicative mood
questions.explanation: The first sentence uses passive voice, while the second uses active voice with Ada as the subject.

questions.prompt: Read this passage: A detailed map was drawn by the cartographer. She labeled every river and mountain range in red ink. What shift occurs between the two sentences?

Active voice to passive voice

questions.skill: Identifying shifts in voice and mood
questions.topic: Notice It in a Model Text - Shifts in Voice and Mood

questions.prompt: Which passage contains both an active-to-passive voice shift and an indicative-to-imperative mood shift?
choices: The gardener planted the herbs. The pots were moved beside the door. The plants need regular watering.
The gardener planted the herbs. The pots stood beside the door. Water them each morning.
The pots were moved by the gardener. The gardener planted the herbs. Water them each morning.
The gardener planted the herbs. The pots were moved beside the door. Water them each morning.

questions.prompt: The veterinarian examined the dog. The owner was given clear instructions. Which option follows the same voice-and-mood pattern as this text?

The hedge was pruned by the gardener. The branches were gathered by workers.

questions.prompt: Read this passage: Turn off the lights before leaving the room. The electricity bill rose sharply last month. What shift in mood occurs between the two sentences?

questions.prompt: Read this model text: The greenhouse was repaired by the volunteer group. The volunteer group replaced several broken panes. Several broken panes needed replacement. choices: The greenhouse was repaired by the volunteer group.
The volunteer group replaced several broken panes.
Several broken panes needed replacement.
The repairs were completed before winter.

questions.prompt: The parcel was sent by the seller. The buyer received it the next day. Which option uses the same sequence of voices as the text?
choices: The clerk sorted the letters. The clerk mailed them on Friday.
The clerk sorted the letters. They were mailed on Friday.
The letters were sorted by the clerk. The clerk mailed them on Friday.
The letters were sorted by the clerk. They were mailed on Friday.

questions.prompt: Read this model text: Volunteers collected donations. The donations were counted in the lobby. Count every donation carefully. What two shifts occur from the first sentence to the second and from the second sentence to the third?

questions.prompt: Model text: Several volunteers collected pledges during the drive. The pledges were sorted by amount at the office. Each donor received a receipt after giving. The campaign team thanked everyone at noon. Which sentence uses passive voice?

questions.prompt: Which sentence pair contains a shift from passive voice to active voice?

questions.topic: Shifts in Voice and Mood in a Model Text

questions.prompt: Read this model text: The mural was painted by the art club. The club received applause from visitors. If the club had not painted it, the wall would have remained plain. Which pair of shifts occurs across the model text?

questions.prompt: Read this model text: Sentence 1: The trail was marked by the park staff. Sentence 2: The staff reminded hikers to pack water. source.claim: The subjunctive mood is used for counterfactual conditionals.
source.quote: For instance, conditionals with a counterfactual or modally remote meaning are sometimes referred to as "counterfactual conditionals".
